Indian Courts Hear Multiple Pleas on Diverse Issues

The Delhi High Court has sought responses from the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regarding a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) challenging the sale of non-dairy paneer and dairy analogue paneer. The PIL notes that Gujarat, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra have already taken steps against such products. Separately, the Delhi High Court asked the Centre for its stance on a plea to regulate protests, citing losses incurred by traders. The court also gave the Delhi police until October 13 to respond to a protest plea filed by the Indian Youth Congress (IYC). Meanwhile, the Supreme Court is scheduled to hear a plea on October 28 challenging changes made by the Election Commission to Form 6 for Delhi's Special Summary Revision, and has advanced a hearing on a plea concerning voter deletion in Delhi to the same date. The Supreme Court has also asked the Centre and states to respond to a PIL seeking a ban on alcohol sales in tetra packs. In other judicial news, the Calcutta High Court requested a report from the State Election Commission (SEC) on EVM and VVPAT shortages ahead of municipal polls, and the Telangana High Court reserved orders on an Amrapali cadre plea. The High Court also put on hold a trial court's order and sought an explanation for delays in deciding a plea.
